## `funcdctl app deploy`

```text
funcdctl app deploy <dir|ref> [flags]

Render an App template, apply the App and wait until its new revision is current or failed.

One command deploys, upgrades and downgrades. Deploy prints the revision it follows and each part whose state changes, and exits 0 once the revision is current; 1 when it fails, when the App's spec changes before it is stamped, or when the App is deleted. The server's app.upgradeTimeout bounds a rollout; an interrupt stops the wait, not the rollout.
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | bool | `false` | admit the App and store nothing; print what the deploy would do and wait for nothing |
| `--name` | string |  | the App's name (default: app.yaml's name) |
| `-n`, `--namespace` | string |  | namespace (default: default) |
| `--no-wait` | bool | `false` | return once the App is applied |
| `--resource-group` | string |  | resource group (default: the App's name, or the stored App's group) |
| `-f`, `--values` | stringArray | `[]` | a values file; repeat it to merge files in order |

## `funcdctl app lock`

```text
funcdctl app lock <dir> [flags]

Resolve each image of an App template to a version and a digest, and write them to its app.lock.

An exact entry resolves its tag; a range takes the highest version tag it accepts. The registry is the template's registry value, from the -f files and the schema defaults. Any failure writes nothing.
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-f`, `--values` | stringArray | `[]` | a values file; repeat it to merge files in order |

## `funcdctl apply`

```text
funcdctl apply [flags]

Apply a manifest of one or more YAML documents, or JSON (- for stdin).

Every document is validated offline first; then the documents are applied in order. Apply stops at the first error the server returns and names that document; the documents before it stay applied.

With --dry-run each document is admitted against the store as it is and nothing is stored: apply prints what it would apply, and an App's plan.
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | bool | `false` | admit each document against the store and store nothing; print what would apply |
| `-f`, `--file` | string |  | manifest file (YAML or JSON); - for stdin |

## `funcdctl backup`

```text
funcdctl backup

Platform backup: status (the daemon's report), verify (off the box) and plan (objectives into settings)
```

## `funcdctl backup plan`

```text
funcdctl backup plan <platform|kv|blob|lake|schedule> [flags]

Print the backup settings recovery objectives give, as an example: --rpo (the most data a loss may take) and --keep (how far back a restore point must reach) give the platform, kv or blob keys of funcdconfig.yaml, or the schedule and ttl of a BackupSchedule (-f); lake says why a Lake needs no key. The example passes the daemon's own loader merged into the located file, then is printed; no file is written. --rto with --size and --speed checks the download time, a lower bound: only a restore drill proves an RTO. Exit 1: refused, nothing printed; 3: the RTO is below the download time.
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--config` | string |  | platform, kv, blob, lake: path to funcdconfig.yaml (else $FUNCD_CONFIG, ./funcdconfig.yaml, /etc/funcd/funcdconfig.yaml) |
| `-f`, `--file` | string |  | schedule: a manifest holding one BackupSchedule; - for stdin |
| `--keep` | string |  | how far back a restore point must reach, a duration (720h) |
| `--rpo` | string |  | the most data a loss may take, a duration (1h) |
| `--rto` | string |  | the target recovery time, a duration; needs --size and --speed |
| `--size` | string |  | the bytes a restore downloads: an integer with an optional Ki, Mi, Gi or Ti suffix |
| `--speed` | string |  | the link's bytes per second, in the grammar of --size |

## `funcdctl backup verify`

```text
funcdctl backup verify [flags]

Check a generation against its manifest, decrypt it to its end and parse its records; with --escrow, also find the keys it names. Then copy it under gen/verified/, manifest last. A generation already pinned is checked again and nothing is written. Run it every (backup.objectives.rpo − backup.interval) / 2.
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--credentials-file` | string |  | s3:// only: the verify credential's AWS shared credentials file |
| `--escrow` | string |  | the escrow set's directory: find the keys the generation names |
| `--generation` | uint64 | `0` | the generation to verify; default the newest complete hourly, daily or weekly one |
| `--identity` | stringArray | `[]` | an age identity file (repeatable) |
| `--target` | string |  | backup.target: s3://… or file:///&lt;absolute dir&gt; |

## `funcdctl completion bash`

```text
funcdctl completion bash

Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(funcdctl completion bash)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	funcdctl completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/funcdctl

#### macOS:

	funcdctl completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/funcdctl

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--no-descriptions` | bool | `false` | disable completion descriptions |

```text

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.
```

## `funcdctl dev`

funcdctl-dev only.

```text
funcdctl dev [dir] [flags]

funcdctl dev runs a folder's resource files from their local builds. A directory that holds app.yaml beside resources/ runs as an App template instead: dev pushes each image's build, renders the template as funcdctl app deploy does and applies the App, then again on each save.

A funcdctl.config.yaml in the current directory holds what dev is run with: its dev keys are these flags in camelCase (dir, values, build, hooks, apply, persist, persistTo, gport, s3port, cport), plus env and envFile for the values of a declared Secret no document defines, and platform for runtime.handOutSettle, eventing.blobPollInterval and funclog.segmentMaxAge. A flag given here replaces its key, and a dir argument replaces dev.dir.

For an App template the file also takes watch, a list of name, run and dir: dev starts each command, waits for the builds they write and keeps their output in log files; and liveReload: true, which reloads open Site pages after a Site change.
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--apply` | stringArray | `[]` | a file of resource documents applied before the App, again when it changes (App mode; repeatable) |
| `--build` | stringArray | `[]` | an App's builds: a folder each image key is looked up in, or &lt;key&gt;=&lt;path&gt; (App mode; repeatable) |
| `--cport` | int | `0` | fixed control-plane port (for `funcdctl --server`: apply, workflow run); 0 ⇒ a random free port |
| `--gport` | int | `0` | fixed gateway (function-invoke) port; 0 ⇒ a random free port |
| `--hooks` | bool | `false` | keep the App's preApply and postApply hooks, called on each new revision (App mode) |
| `--persist` | bool | `false` | persist KV/blob/metastore to a local dir between runs (default: ephemeral in-memory) |
| `--persist-to` | string | `.funcd-dev` | directory for --persist state (per-service subdirs: metastore/kv/blob) |
| `--print-env` | bool | `false` | print the dev S3 credentials as `export …` lines and exit (no server); pair with a fixed --s3port. Use: eval "$(funcdctl dev &lt;dir&gt; --s3port 3006 --print-env)" |
| `--s3port` | int | `0` | fixed S3-frontend port; 0 ⇒ a random free port |
| `-f`, `--values` | stringArray | `[]` | an App template's values file; repeat it to merge files in order (App mode) |

## `funcdctl push`

```text
funcdctl push <path> <ref> [flags]

Package a function (a file or a bundle directory) — or, with --site, a prebuilt static web app, or with --template, an App template — as an OCI artifact and push it (prints <ref>@<digest>)
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--entry` | string |  | handler entry file relative to the bundle root (directory push only); default main.py for a python runtime, else main.mjs |
| `--platform` | string |  | the platform the artifact was built for (linux/amd64 or linux/arm64), recorded on the manifest so `funcdctl index` can combine per-platform pushes |
| `--site` | bool | `false` | push &lt;path&gt; (a directory) as a static-site bundle for a Site: one deterministic tar+gzip layer, no contract/runtime/entry |
| `--template` | bool | `false` | push &lt;path&gt; (an App template directory with a fresh app.lock) as it is, tagged with its version |

## `funcdctl quarantine return`

```text
funcdctl quarantine return <kvstore|bucket|volume> <namespace>/<name>[/<volume>] [flags]

Return an object's quarantined data into it. Apply the object again first: the return refuses an object that is missing or whose data is not empty, and nothing returns on its own. A volume is <namespace>/<function>/<volume>. Without --since, the newest entry returns; a return cut short resumes when run again.
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--since` | string |  | the entry's since, as hold status lists it (RFC 3339); the newest entry when absent |

| `--input` | string |  | run input: inline JSON or @file (default: empty) |
| `-n`, `--namespace` | string |  | namespace (default: default) |
| `--resource-group` | string | `default` | resource group |

## `funcdctl workflow runs`

```text
funcdctl workflow runs [flags]

List workflow runs (newest first; --phase to filter)
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-n`, `--namespace` | string |  | namespace (default: default) |
| `-o`, `--output` | string |  | output format: json |
| `--phase` | string |  | filter by run phase (Pending\|Running\|Paused\|Succeeded\|Failed\|Cancelled) |
